market_commentary:
WTI crude settled at US$102.88/bbl on March 31 — its first weekly close above $100 since July 2022 — as the Strait of Hormuz closure, in effect since approximately March 2, continued to disrupt an estimated 20 million barrels per day of seaborne oil flows.1 Brent crude rose to US$112.78/bbl, recording its largest monthly percentage gain since contract inception in 1988.2 The TSX Composite closed the week at 32,427, gaining 1.54% on March 31, though the index declined approximately 6% over the full month of March.3 Gold fell to approximately US$4,578/oz, its steepest monthly decline since October 2008, while the Bank of Canada held its overnight rate at 2.25% following seven consecutive cuts from the June 2024 peak of 5.00%.45

The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine links 63 oil and gas projects to the current WTI price environment, with 727 Alberta projects in the database carrying direct commodity exposure to crude price movements.6 If WTI holds above $100/bbl, the database's oil and gas projects — concentrated in Alberta oil sands and Saskatchewan heavy oil — would maintain price levels above the breakeven thresholds reported in public project filings. The 364 mining projects in the database carry exposure to gold's 14% monthly price decline; the database recorded a peak price of US$5,161/oz on March 3 before the month-end closing of US$4,578.7 The Government of Canada yield curve maintained a normal shape with the 2-year/10-year spread at 63 basis points, placing the 1,034 under-construction projects in the database within a broadly stable long-term financing rate environment.8
